# Ileocøkal resektion

Ileocøkal resektion is a surgical procedure for [[crohns-disease|Crohn's disease]] that represents a significant intervention in the long-term management of the condition. The procedure is performed on approximately 75% of Crohn's disease patients over the course of their illness [^src1], making it a common and clinically important intervention. Beyond the surgery itself, postoperative endoscopic follow-up is a critical component of care after ileocøkal resektion.

According to the Danish quality registry for inflammatory bowel disease (DANIBD), 179 adult patients with Crohn's disease underwent ileocøkal resektion during a recent audit period [^src2]. This volume reflects the procedure's prevalence in the management of Crohn's disease, though regional variation in postoperative care quality suggests inconsistency in follow-up protocols across Denmark. The DANIBD quality indicator monitoring ileocøkal resektion specifically tracks the proportion of adult Crohn's disease patients who receive the recommended endoscopic follow-up within one year of surgery—a metric that reveals significant regional disparities in adherence to clinical guidelines [^src1].

The quality of postoperative care following ileocøkal resektion varies markedly across Danish regions. Nationally, 65% of patients achieved the recommended endoscopic follow-up within one year, falling short of the 80% development target. Region Syddanmark was the only region that met this target, underscoring both the feasibility of achieving guideline-concordant care and the systemic challenges in other parts of the country [^src1].
